---
title: "The label audit and test-clean"
subtitle: "When the gold answer is the problem"
---

{{< include /_setup.qmd >}}

```{python}
from collections import Counter

audited = len(audit)
verdict_counts = Counter(r["verdict"] for r in audit)
categories = Counter(r["category"] for r in audit if r["category"])
unsound = verdict_counts["label_ambiguous"] + verdict_counts["label_wrong"]
```

Before any training, the baselines' mistakes looked suspicious: models of 0.8B, 2B and 4B parameters
made about the same number of wrong-argument errors. Errors that don't shrink with a model five
times larger point at the answers, not the models. Is "3% interest" `3` or `0.03`?

So every test row that **any** baseline got wrong was audited, `{python} n(audited)` of the
`{python} n(splits["test"])`, most of them by hand, with one question: *would a careful
person, reading only the query and the tool specs, write this gold answer?* Labelling was blind to
which model erred.

::: {.column-margin}
The rubric: [docs/label-audit.md](https://github.com/joaomigueloliveira/qwen-function-calling-distillation/blob/main/docs/label-audit.md).
Why test labels are never edited:
[ADR 0002](../decisions/0002-test-labels-never-edited.html).
:::

## What it found

| Verdict | Rows |
|---|---:|
| Sound: what a careful person would write | `{python} n(verdict_counts["label_sound"])` |
| Ambiguous: one reasonable answer among several | `{python} n(verdict_counts["label_ambiguous"])` |
| Wrong: contradicts the query or specs, or makes a value up | `{python} n(verdict_counts["label_wrong"])` |

The most common reasons, among the audited rows:

```{python}
labels = {
    "unclear units or format": "a format the spec leaves open (`UK` or `GB`, casing)",
    "default made explicit": "gold and a model differ only by an optional argument at its default",
    "underspecified query": "the query doesn't fix the value (\"last week\", with no date)",
    "wrong value": "a wrong or made-up value (`YOUR_API_KEY`)",
}
Markdown(
    "| Reason | Rows |\n|---|---:|\n"
    + "\n".join(f"| {labels.get(c, c)} | {categories[c]:,} |" for c, _ in categories.most_common(4))
)
```

## test-clean

**test-clean** is test without the ambiguous and wrong rows: `{python} n(splits["test-clean"])`
rows. It is where methods are compared, and it tells a different story from raw test: a method
can gain on raw test by learning gold's quirks, such as which of two reasonable answers xLAM chose.
The `{python} n(unsound)` unsound rows are a lower bound, since rows every model got right are
assumed sound.

Test's labels are never edited, so numbers on raw test stay comparable with other work. Train and
validation keep their noise too: removing it would take judgement no rule captures, and the
teacher's answers, which the label-free methods train on, never read gold anyway.

::: {.column-margin}
Train and validation keep their label noise:
[ADR 0005](../decisions/0005-train-and-validation-keep-label-noise.html). The full audit:
[results/label-audit.md](https://github.com/joaomigueloliveira/qwen-function-calling-distillation/blob/main/results/label-audit.md).
:::
